title: लाहुरी भैंसी कथामा चेतन र अचेतन वस्तुवक्रता Lahuri bhainsi kathama chetan ra achetan bastubakrata
nepali: रमेश विकलद्वारा रचित लाहुरी भैँसी कथाको प्रायोगिक अध्ययन संस्कृतका आचार्य कुन्तकद्वारा प्रतिपादित वक्रोक्तिसिद्धान्तको चेतन वस्तु र अचेतन वस्तुवक्रताका आधारमा गरिएको छ । यस लेखमा चेतन वस्तु र अचेतन वस्तुवक्रताको सैद्धान्तिक पर्याधार अनुरूप बनाइएको विश्लेषणको ढाँचाअनुसार शोध्य कृतिबाट चेतन वस्तु र अचेतन वस्तु एवम् तिनका विभिन्न उपकरणसँग सम्बद्ध सामग्री सङ्कलन गरी तिनको विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । यसमा सर्वप्रथम चेतन वस्तुवक्रतासँग सम्बद्ध सामग्रीमा प्रस्तुत कथाका प्रमुख पात्र लुखुरे र द्वारेको मानसिक व्यापार, समाख्याताको दृष्टिकोण, पात्रहरूको भौतिक अवस्था र सोचाइबाट उत्पन्न अन्तद्र्वन्द्वसँग सम्बद्ध सामग्रीको विश्लेषणबाट उत्पन्न सौन्दर्र्य खोजिएकोे छ । अचेतन वस्तुवक्रतामा घटनाको स्थानिक र कालिक स्थिति, गालीगलौज र अपमानबोधक सामाजिक परिवेश, देवीदेवताको पुकार र मान्यजनप्रतिको सम्मानबोधक सांस्कृतिक स्थिति, गरिबप्रति सामन्तको थिचोमिचो जनाउने सामन्ती व्यवहारका कार्यबाट चेतन वस्तुको मनस्थिति प्रभावित भएका सम्बद्ध प्रमाण खोजी तिनका आधारमा अचेतन वस्तुवक्रताको सौन्दर्य केलाइएको छ । त्यस्तै चेतन वस्तुका कार्यकलापमा प्रभाव पार्ने गरी गौण चेतन वस्तु (मानवेतर पात्र) लाहुरी भैँसीको चित्रणबाट लुखुरे र द्वारेका मनमा परेका प्रभावको चित्रण पनि प्रस्तुत कथामा फरकफरक किसिमबाट गरिएको छ । यसरी प्रस्तुत कथामा चेतन वस्तुका कार्यकलापलाई उद्वेलित तुल्याउने गरी गौण चेतन वस्तु र अचेतन वस्तुका विविध पक्षको वर्णन गरिएकाले विश्लेष्य कथा चेतन वस्तु, अचेतन वस्तु र गौण चेतन वस्तुवक्रताका दृष्टिले कलात्मक रहेको निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ ।
american_english: An applied study of the short story 'Lahuri Bhainsi,' written by Ramesh Vikal, has been conducted on the basis of sentient-object and insentient-object obliqueness within the Vakrokti theory propounded by the Sanskrit scholar Acharya Kuntaka. In this article, following an analytical framework constructed in accordance with the theoretical foundation of sentient-object and insentient-object obliqueness, material related to sentient objects, insentient objects, and their various devices has been collected from the studied work and analyzed. In this, first of all, within the material associated with sentient-object obliqueness, the aesthetic beauty emerging from the analysis of material related to the mental transactions of the story's main characters Lukhure and Dware, the narrator's viewpoint, and the inner conflict arising from the characters' physical condition and thoughts has been sought. In insentient-object obliqueness, the aesthetic beauty of insentient-object obliqueness has been examined on the basis of seeking relevant evidence showing how the mindset of sentient entities was affected by the spatial and temporal setting of events, a social milieu marked by verbal abuse and humiliation, a cultural state reflecting invocations of deities and respect toward elders, and acts of feudal behavior demonstrating the oppression of the poor by feudal masters. Similarly, so as to influence the activities of sentient beings, the depiction of the impact produced on the minds of Lukhure and Dware through the portrayal of the secondary sentient object (a non-human character), the Lahuri buffalo, has also been carried out in distinct ways in the present story. Thus, because diverse aspects of secondary sentient objects and insentient objects are described in the present story in such a way as to agitate the activities of sentient beings, it is concluded that the analyzed story is artistic from the perspectives of sentient-object, insentient-object, and secondary sentient-object obliqueness.

informal_english: This applied study of the short story 'Lahuri Bhainsi,' written by Ramesh Vikal, is carried out on the basis of sentient-object and insentient-object obliqueness from the Vakrokti theory propounded by Sanskrit scholar Acharya Kuntaka. In this, first off, within the material to do with sentient-object obliqueness, the aesthetic beauty coming out of sorting through the headspace of the story's main characters Lukhure and Dware, the narrator's take, and the inner conflict stirred up by the characters' physical state and thinking has been looked into. As for insentient-object obliqueness, the aesthetic beauty of insentient-object obliqueness has been weighed up by tracking down evidence of how the mindset of sentient entities was rattled by the time and place of events, a rough social setting full of cursing and put-downs, a cultural scene calling on deities and showing respect to elders, and feudal behaviour showing the oppression of the poor by feudal masters. Likewise, so as to sway what sentient beings get up to, the depiction of the impact made on the minds of Lukhure and Dware through showing the secondary sentient object (a non-human character)—the Lahuri buffalo—has also been handled in quite different ways in the present story. Thus, because various aspects of secondary sentient objects and insentient objects are described in the present story in a way that really stirs up the activities of sentient beings, the wrap-up is that the analysed story is proper artistic from the angles of sentient-object, insentient-object, and secondary sentient-object obliqueness.
translator_notes: Sanskrit poetics terms from Kuntaka's Vakrokti theory (chetan vastu vakrata, achetan vastu vakrata, gauna chetan vastu) rendered as sentient-object, insentient-object, and secondary sentient-object obliqueness/obliquity. Characters Lukhure and Dware, and story title 'Lahuri Bhainsi' transliterated. Strict 6-sentence order maintained across all variants. Informal flavour: New Zealand casual.
